title: A second buy on a held symbol silently destroys the earlier position — capital vanishes from the book; flat market reports -3.0% total return
repro: sidecar/.venv/bin/python, fixture loader, a strategy that returns BacktestOrderIntent(qty=+10) on every bar without gating on has_position: 4 bars at a flat close of 100, initialCapital 100000. Result: 4 trade rows recorded, cash correctly debited 4 x 1001 = 4004, but portfolio.positions['AAA'] holds 10 shares not 40 -> final equity 96996 and metrics.totalReturn = -0.03004 on a market that never moved. The three orphaned entry rows keep pnl=None forever, so tradeCount/winRate never see them.
evidence: sidecar/services/backtest_engine.py:343 (`portfolio.positions[intent.symbol] = _OpenPosition(...)` — assignment, not merge), sidecar/services/backtest_engine.py:324 (comment directly above reads `# New long position OR add to existing`), sidecar/services/backtest_engine.py:114-118 (equity marks only the surviving position)
notes: Pull-complexity-downward violation (APOSD 7) with a comment asserting the opposite of the code (APOSD 11). Unreachable from the four bundled strategies only because each one self-gates on has_position (backtest_strategies.py:262,341,414; backtest_dsl.py:703) — an invariant repeated at four call sites that the engine could hold once. register_strategy (backtest_engine.py:144) is public extension surface, so the first plugin or agent-authored strategy that pyramids hits this. Smallest fix: on buy, merge into the existing _OpenPosition with a weighted-average entry price instead of replacing it.

refuter.reason: Mechanism confirmed (buy assigns a fresh _OpenPosition, orphaning the earlier one while cash stays debited, under a comment claiming 'add to existing'), but it is unreachable in the shipped product: register_strategy is only called by register_all for four strategies, all of which gate entries on has_position, and plugins have no backtest-strategy registration path. Latent maintainer trap, not a core flow that breaks today -> medium.

title: Selling more than is held mints cash — a sell intent larger than the position is credited in full and pops the whole position

Result: final equity 108989 from initialCapital 100000 on a market that never moved; the trade's reported pnl is -19.99 (fees only), so nothing in the trade log or metrics hints that 90 phantom shares were sold.
evidence: sidecar/services/backtest_engine.py:362-365 (position looked up, then `portfolio.cash += abs(intent.quantity) * fill_price` with no reconciliation against position.quantity), sidecar/services/backtest_engine.py:371 (pnl computed on abs(intent.quantity)), sidecar/services/backtest_engine.py:385 (`portfolio.positions.pop(...)` regardless of size), sidecar/services/backtest_engine.py:368-370 (comment parks the partial-close case as a 'documented limitation')

Smallest fix: qty = min(abs(intent.quantity), position.quantity); credit and compute pnl on qty; pop only when the remainder reaches 0.

refuter.reason: Mechanism confirmed (sell credits abs(intent.quantity) with no reconciliation against position.quantity, then pops the whole position), but, as with COD-backtest-3, every registered strategy exits with quantity=-held, so no shipped path (UI, custom DSL, agent tool) can over-sell. Latent -> medium.

title: consumeSseStream draws the protocol/consumer boundary wrong twice: consumer exceptions are relabelled 'unparseable SSE frame', and an EOF with no done/error frame is silent success
repro: design: handlers.onEvent(event) is inside the same try as JSON.parse (streaming.ts:263-271). A throw in ChatSidebar's onToolUse/enqueueChange or in feedBriefLifecycle (called from normalizeEvent) is caught, relabelled `unparseable SSE frame: <consumer message>`, routed to onError -> the assistant message is failed and the run ended as 'error' while the stream keeps delivering frames to a settled message. SECOND HALF (design): consumeSseStream returns normally when reader.read() reports done (streaming.ts:225-244) whether or not a terminal frame was seen; ChatSidebar settles a turn ONLY in onDone/onError (ChatSidebar.tsx:890-939) and does nothing after `await streamAgentInvocation(...)` (:1005-1038). Any server path that closes the generator without `done` leaves the message 'streaming', the rail run 'running', abortRef held and the brief panel in_flight, forever.
evidence: src/modules/chat/streaming.ts:263-271, src/modules/chat/streaming.ts:302-305 (store side effect inside normalizeEvent), src/modules/chat/ChatSidebar.tsx:890-912, src/modules/chat/streaming.ts:225-249 (no sawTerminal tracking), src/modules/chat/ChatSidebar.tsx:914-939,1005-1038, src/modules/chat/streaming.test.ts (10 tests; none for non-ok, malformed frame, consumer throw, or EOF-without-done)
notes: Exception aggregation at the wrong boundary: a protocol error and a consumer bug get one label, so the next maintainer debugs the wire for a UI defect. Related obviousness smell: `normalizeEvent` reads as a pure snake->camel mapper but mutates the brief store. Smallest fix: try only around JSON.parse/normalizeEvent; call onEvent outside it; move feedBriefLifecycle to dispatchFrame after normalisation. For the EOF half: the invariant 'every stream ends in done|error' is held by convention on the server (each adapter + two router guards remember to yield done) when three client lines can hold it structurally: track `sawTerminal` in dispatchFrame and, after the read loop, call onError(new Error('The stream ended before the answer finished.')) if it is false.

refuter.reason: Holds on both halves: dispatchFrame wraps JSON.parse, normalizeEvent (which calls feedBriefLifecycle) and handlers.onEvent in one try and relabels any throw 'unparseable SSE frame: …'; consumeSseStream returns normally on reader done without tracking a terminal frame, and ChatSidebar settles only in onDone/onError with nothing after the await.

title: Concurrent quant requests corrupt each other through QuantLib's process-global evaluation date
repro: Two threads call services.quant._common.set_evaluation_date with different dates then read ql.Settings.instance().evaluationDate: thread A set 2026-05-16, thread B set 2030-01-02, both observe 'January 2nd, 2030'. The four /quant routes are plain sync `def`, so FastAPI runs them concurrently in the anyio worker threadpool -> two simultaneous pricing calls with different valuation_date can each be served the other's date.
evidence: sidecar/services/quant/_common.py:34-41 (set_evaluation_date writes the process global), _common.py:57 (build_bsm_process calls it on every price), sidecar/services/quant/bonds.py:52 and sidecar/services/quant/yield_curve.py:70 (write it directly), sidecar/routers/quant.py:37,46,55,64 (all four routes are sync `def`, unlike routers/macro.py:47,60,72 which are async def)
notes: QuantLib Settings is a process singleton, not thread-local (proved by the two-thread probe). Response is a 200 with a plausible price; there is no detection, no log line and no test. Aggravating: sidecar/services/agent_tools/quant_tools.py:42-101 are async def but call options.price(...) SYNCHRONOUSLY on the event loop, and models/quant.py:33 permits binomial_steps up to 100_000, which _greeks_fd re-prices 9 times - one agent tool call blocks every other sidecar request for the duration. Smallest fix: a module-level threading.Lock in _common.py wrapping set-date-through-price as one critical section, plus await asyncio.to_thread(...) in the four quant_tools handlers. Neither touches the wire contract.

refuter.reason: Mechanism is real and worse than a date mix-up: the four /quant routes are sync def (threadpool) and every engine writes the process-global ql.Settings evaluationDate before a lazy NPV(); a two-thread probe returned price 0.0 (option judged already expired) for 1413 of 3000 pricings of a valid ITM-ish call when a second thread priced with a later valuation date. Severity corrected critical->high only because the trigger needs two overlapping quant computations with DIFFERENT valuation dates in a single-user desktop (panel computes are click-driven; the async agent tools call options.price synchronously on the event loop, quant_tools.py:54, which also blocks the loop for large binomial_steps).
